story.head: A good test for both
paras: The Wild won the teams’ first meeting this season, 4-1 in Minnesota on Oct 3. The Bruins (13-5-1) lost 5-2 to Montréal on Thursday, while the Wild have won two in a row. Two good teams meet. Going in, the Wild are first in the Central (tied for first in the NHL) and the Bruins third in the Atlantic (tied for eighth).

The Wild’s record (.762) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.652), largely thanks to their goaltending. So is the Bruins’ (.711 on chances worth .562), largely thanks to their goaltending.

The Bruins (lowest) and the Wild (3rd lowest) both leave the shooting to their forwards. The Wild let the point shots come and guard the net (2nd) and get pinned in their own end on long shifts (32nd). Minnesota has allowed 2.19 goals a game, the fewest in the league. As for the Bruins, they have had some of the league’s best goaltending (2nd). They also sit back rather than chase on the forecheck (2nd lowest), so the Wild hound the puck, but them sit back. Boston has allowed 2.42 goals a game, the third fewest in the league. The Bruins’ good looks will be harder to come by against the Wild.

Kirill Kaprizov (17 G / 18 A / 35 P in 21 GP) leads the Wild in scoring and is third in the NHL, with ten points in his last five games and a point in five straight games against Boston. Quinn Hughes (6 G / 22 A / 28 P in 21 GP) isn’t far behind, with seven points in his last five games. For the Bruins, David Pastrňák (8 G / 16 A / 24 P in 19 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Elias Lindholm (7 G / 10 A / 17 P in 19 GP) is next in line.

Jesper Wallstedt (13-2-3 / .925 SV% in 18 GS) has been outstanding for Minnesota and will likely start. Jeremy Swayman (9-4-1 / .913 SV% in 14 GS) has been outstanding for Boston and will likely start.
At home, Marco Sturm likes to send Mittelstadt, Lindholm and Khusnutdinov out against the other team’s top line, so watch for them against Kaprizov, Ek and Boldy.

items.text: The Wild have been without Filip Gustavsson all season. Jesper Wallstedt is expected to start.
The Bruins are newly without James Hagens, and have been without Connor Clifton since Oct 29.
Joel Eriksson Ek has five goals on chances worth about 10.5 goals, well below what his finishing usually turns chances into. If the chances keep coming, so should the goals.
Kirill Kaprizov and Quinn Hughes have a point in ten straight games.
